nodes.summary: For every $x = a + b\sqrt{-2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$, the norm $N(x) = a^2 + 2b^2$ satisfies $|N(x)| = N(x)$, where $|N(x)|$ is taken as a natural number and read back as an integer.
nodes.title: The norm on $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$ equals its absolute value

nodes.summary: Let $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ with $y = c + d\sqrt{-2}$, let $\bar{y} = c - d\sqrt{-2}$ be its conjugate and $N(y) = c^2 + 2d^2$ its norm, and write $x\bar{y} = u + v\sqrt{-2}$ with $u, v \in \mathbb{Z}$. The quotient is $x / y = \operatorname{round}(u / N(y)) + \operatorname{round}(v / N(y))\sqrt{-2}$, where $u / N(y)$ and $v / N(y)$ are computed in $\mathbb{Q}$ (division by $0$ gives $0$) and…
nodes.title: Rounding division on $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$

nodes.summary: For all $x, y$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$, the remainder is $x \bmod y = x - y\,(x / y)$, where $x / y$ is the rounding division of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$.
nodes.title: Remainder of the rounding division on $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$

nodes.summary: Let $x, y$ be elements of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ with $y \ne 0$, and let $N(a + b\sqrt{-2}) = a^2 + 2b^2$ be the norm. The remainder $x \bmod y = x - y\,(x / y)$ of the rounding division of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ satisfies $|N(x \bmod y)| < |N(y)|$ as natural numbers.
nodes.title: The remainder is smaller than the divisor, in absolute norm

nodes.summary: For $x = a + b\sqrt{-2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ with norm $N(x) = a^2 + 2b^2$, we have $N(x) = 0$ if and only if $x = 0$.
nodes.title: The norm on $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$ vanishes only at zero

nodes.summary: Let $x, y, q \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$, write $N(a + b\sqrt{-2}) = a^2 + 2b^2$ for the norm and $\bar{y}$ for the conjugate of $y$, and write $x\bar{y} = u + v\sqrt{-2}$ and $q = e + f\sqrt{-2}$ with $u, v, e, f \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then $N(y)\,N(x - yq) = (u - N(y)\,e)^2 + 2\,(v - N(y)\,f)^2$.
nodes.title: Norm identity for the remainder

nodes.summary: Let $N(a + b\sqrt{-2}) = a^2 + 2b^2$ be the norm on $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$. For $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ with $y \ne 0$, we have $|N(x)| \le |N(xy)|$ as natural numbers.
nodes.title: Multiplying by a nonzero element does not decrease the norm in $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$

nodes.summary: Let $x, y$ be elements of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ with $y \ne 0$, and let $N(a + b\sqrt{-2}) = a^2 + 2b^2$ be the norm. The remainder $x \bmod y = x - y\,(x / y)$ of the rounding division of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ satisfies $N(x \bmod y) < N(y)$.
nodes.title: The remainder is smaller than the divisor in $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$

nodes.summary: For every $x = a + b\sqrt{-2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$, the norm $N(x) = a^2 + 2b^2$ satisfies $N(x) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: The norm on $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$ is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For $x = a + b\sqrt{-2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ with norm $N(x) = a^2 + 2b^2$, we have $N(x) > 0$ if and only if $x \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Nonzero elements of $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$ have positive norm

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $N$ be integers with $N > 0$, and let $q$ be the integer nearest to the rational number $a/N$ (halves rounded up). Then $|2(a - qN)| \le N$, that is, $a$ differs from $qN$ by at most $N/2$.
nodes.title: Error of rounded integer division

nodes.summary: Let $\varepsilon_0 = 1$ and $\varepsilon_1 = -1$ be the enumeration of the units of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$. Every unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ equals $\varepsilon_i$ for some $i \in \{0, 1\}$.
nodes.title: Every unit of ℤ(√−2) is enumerated

nodes.summary: Let $\varepsilon_0 = 1$ and $\varepsilon_1 = -1$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$. For $i, j \in \{0, 1\}$, if $\varepsilon_i = \varepsilon_j$ then $i = j$.
nodes.title: The enumeration of the units of ℤ(√−2) is injective

nodes.summary: The map $\{0, 1\} \to \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ sending $0$ to $1$ and $1$ to $-1$. Since $1$ and $-1$ are their own inverses, its value at $i$ is the inverse of the $i$-th enumerated unit.
nodes.title: Inverses of the enumerated units of ℤ(√−2)

nodes.summary: Let $\varepsilon_0 = 1$, $\varepsilon_1 = -1$ be the enumerated units of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ and $\eta_0 = 1$, $\eta_1 = -1$ their listed inverses. Then $\varepsilon_i \eta_i = 1$ for each $i \in \{0, 1\}$.
nodes.title: Each enumerated unit of ℤ(√−2) times its listed inverse is one

nodes.summary: The map $\{0, 1\} \to \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ sending $0$ to $1$ and $1$ to $-1$, which lists the two units of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$.
nodes.title: Enumeration of the units of ℤ(√−2)

nodes.summary: If $p$ is a prime number with $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$ or $p \equiv 7 \pmod 8$, then $p$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$.
nodes.title: Primes congruent to 5 or 7 mod 8 are inert in ℤ(√−2)

nodes.summary: An element $x$ of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ is a unit if and only if $x = 1$ or $x = -1$.
nodes.title: Units of ℤ(√−2)

nodes.summary: For all $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}/8\mathbb{Z}$, $x^2 + 2y^2 \ne 5$ and $x^2 + 2y^2 \ne 7$.
nodes.title: x² + 2y² is never 5 or 7 modulo 8

nodes.summary: For $\pi = a + b\sqrt{-2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ let $N(\pi) = a^2 + 2b^2$ be its norm. If $|N(\pi)|$ is a prime number, then $\pi$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$.
nodes.title: Elements of ℤ(√−2) of prime norm are prime

nodes.summary: The element $\sqrt{-2}$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$.
nodes.title: √−2 is prime in ℤ(√−2)

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime number and let $\pi = a + b\sqrt{-2}$ be an element of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ whose norm $a^2 + 2b^2$ equals $p$. Write $\bar\pi = a - b\sqrt{-2}$ for the conjugate of $\pi$. Then $p = \pi\bar\pi$, $\bar\pi$ is prime in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$, and $\bar\pi$ is not associated to $\pi$.
nodes.title: Conjugate factorization of an odd prime in $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime number with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 8$ or $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$. Then there is a prime element $\pi = a + b\sqrt{-2}$ of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ whose norm $a^2 + 2b^2$ equals $p$.
nodes.title: Primes $p \equiv 1, 3 \pmod 8$ are norms of primes of $\mathbb{Z}(\sqrt{-2})$

nodes.summary: In $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-2}]$ one has $2 = -(\sqrt{-2})^2$.
nodes.title: $2$ is minus the square of $\sqrt{-2}$
Number Theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
